main_body: Tall narrow strip made of two columns: a left column of stacked square wooden blocks (tan top, orange face) and a right column of dark vertical wooden posts with thin grey horizontal rails at rows 15, 31 and 47.
top_band: Left column: light tan band about 2-3 rows at the top of each block, then orange face. Right post column: none, the posts start straight into vertical dark grain; the grey rails are only 2 rows thick.
evidence: The posts are drawn as flat vertical grain with no visible top surface. The grey rails are thin 2-row strips with no readable top face and no set-back front. The left blocks have only a thin tan cap over a flat face, with no front-edge line or eave shadow. The overall construction reads as a front elevation with a thin rim, not a 3/4 frame with horizontal beams and a base showing top faces.

style.evidence: The wood uses about 4 tonal steps with a dark brown, material-tinted outline, which is fine. The post column has large flat dark vertical stripes and the grey rails are flat fills with no texture. Each tile carries fewer colours than the stall and well references, so it reads thinner and flatter than them.
